subtitulo: Bring something small, arrive on time even though nobody else will, and let the host lead the first toast
cena: You've just been invited to someone's home for dinner tonight, and the whole evening hinges on what you do in the next thirty seconds.
decisao: o que levar e a que horas chegar — gastar dez minutos e um valor pequeno numa lembrança, e tratar o horário como compromisso real, decide como a noite inteira começa
frasePiso: Show up with something small, on time, and let them lead the toast. That's the whole shape of the evening.

fatosDatados.afirmacao: It's customary to bring a small gift when invited to someone's home for a meal — flowers, wine, a dessert or something for the children if the hosts have them; avoid yellow flowers (associated with death) or purple flowers (associated with funerals).
fatosDatados.fonte: Consenso de guias culturais (Cultural Atlas, International Living, Mexperience)

fatosDatados.afirmacao: Despite a generally relaxed approach to time, arriving on time to someone's home when invited for a meal is considered a sign of respect for the host's effort.
fatosDatados.fonte: Consenso de guias culturais (International Living, Mexperience)

steps.pt: A home invitation is a real gesture. Three small moves make you a good guest: something small, on time, let the host lead the toast.

steps.es: ¿Te gustaría cenar en mi casa el sábado?
steps.pt: Would you like to have dinner at my place on Saturday?
steps.tts: ¿Te gustaría cenar en mi casa el sábado?

steps.promptPt: Accept the invitation warmly. Speak now.
steps.es: Claro que sí, con mucho gusto.
steps.pinyin: KLAH-roh keh see, kohn MOO-choh GOOS-toh
steps.tts: Claro que sí, con mucho gusto.

steps.pt: Don't arrive empty-handed — flowers, wine, a dessert are the norm. Skip yellow flowers, which read as mourning here.

steps.promptPt: At the door, hand over the small gift you brought. Speak now.
steps.es: Le traje esto para la casa.
steps.pinyin: leh TRAH-heh EHS-toh PAH-rah lah KAH-sah
steps.pt: I brought you this for the house.
steps.tts: Le traje esto para la casa.

steps.es: No te hubieras molestado, muchas gracias.
steps.pt: You didn't have to, thank you so much.
steps.tts: No te hubieras molestado, muchas gracias.

steps.pt: Everything else about time can be relaxed — this isn't. On time for a home invitation reads as respect for the work tonight.

steps.es: Pasa, siéntete como en tu casa.
steps.pt: Come in, make yourself at home.
steps.tts: Pasa, siéntete como en tu casa.

steps.promptPt: Thank them for having you. Speak now.

steps.pt: Glasses fill, the host leads the first toast — you don't invent one. One word is the whole reply.

steps.promptPt: The host raises a glass. Answer the toast. Speak now.
The highest compliment you can pay a home cook. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can you give me the recipe?

steps.promptPt: Plates are moving and you are sitting. Offer. Speak now.
Asking for seconds is itself a compliment here. Speak now.
steps.es: ¿Me da un poco más, por favor?
steps.pinyin: meh dah oon POH-koh mahs por fah-BOR
steps.pt: Could I have a little more, please?
steps.tts: ¿Me da un poco más, por favor?

steps.promptPt: Before the next invitation, check. Speak now.
steps.pinyin: eye AHL-goh keh noh DEH-bah trah-EHR
steps.pt: Is there anything I should not bring?

steps.es: Claro que sí, con mucho gusto. Le traje esto para la casa. Gracias por invitarme.
steps.pinyin: KLAH-roh keh see, kohn MOO-choh GOOS-toh. leh TRAH-heh EHS-toh PAH-rah lah KAH-sah. GRAH-syahs por een-bee-TAHR-meh
steps.pt: Shadow accepting, arriving with a gift, and thanking your host.
steps.tts: Claro que sí, con mucho gusto. Le traje esto para la casa. Gracias por invitarme.

steps.pt: I08 complete. Something small, arrive on time — the clock doesn't relax here — let the host lead the toast, salud replies.

secoes.titulo: The gift is about the gesture, not the value
secoes.corpo: Flowers, wine or something sweet are all normal. What matters is arriving with something in hand, not the price of it — and steering clear of yellow or purple flowers, which read as funeral colours.

secoes.titulo: Punctuality here is specific, not a national rule
secoes.corpo: Mexican time in general has a well-known relaxed reputation, but a home invitation for a meal is treated differently: the host has timed the cooking, and arriving on time respects that effort.

secoes.titulo: Salud is the whole toast reply
secoes.corpo: You don't need a speech back. The host leads; you raise your glass and say salud. That's a complete, warm response.

permissao: You are allowed to show up with something simple and inexpensive. Nobody is judging the gift itself — the gesture of not arriving empty-handed is what actually matters, not the price tag.
espelho: Never showing up to a dinner party empty-handed is a rule most people already follow at home without thinking about it — the only genuinely new piece here is that punctuality matters more for this specific occasion than it might for other plans in the same trip.

fichasCulturais.sinal: You've heard that time runs relaxed in Mexico, so you show up twenty minutes late to a home dinner invitation, the way you might to a casual meetup with friends.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: This is normal and expected, the same as everywhere else time seems flexible here.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: A relaxed general attitude toward time coexists with real expectations around specific occasions — and a home-cooked meal someone has timed and prepared for you is exactly the kind of occasion where punctuality reads as respect, not rigidity.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Treat a home dinner invitation like an appointment with a real time, and arrive on time or very close to it.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You show up when the food is actually ready, and your host doesn't have to manage a cooling meal or a stalled evening.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not a rule for every social plan — a casual meetup at a bar or a loosely arranged outing genuinely does run on a more relaxed clock; it's specifically the hosted, home-cooked invitation where the expectation tightens.
